name: save-my-prompts
description: Improve prompts, turn a good conversation into a reusable template, and save, find and reuse your prompts in ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription:
Save My Prompts is a library for the prompts you use more than once. This app connects it to ChatGPT.

What you can do:
- Improve a prompt. ChatGPT rewrites it with a role, audience, tone, structure and length, and a card shows the new version and what changed.
- Turn a conversation into a template. When something worked, ChatGPT writes a reusable prompt with {{VARIABLES}} for the parts that change.
- Save a prompt to your library, when you ask or click Save on a card. Saving an improved prompt also keeps your original text as its first version.
- Find your saved prompts by words in the title, text or tags, and use one in the chat.
- Reuse what fits. For a bigger task, ChatGPT may check your saved prompts for one that fits, say so in one line, and use it with your details filled in.
- Learn what works. When you say a saved prompt gave a good or a bad result, ChatGPT can record it, so the prompts that work come first.

What data the app receives: ChatGPT sends only what its model passes to a tool, such as the prompt to improve or save, the template it wrote, your search words, or a short description of the task when it checks for a fitting saved prompt. Your whole conversation is not sent. Improving a prompt or writing a template saves nothing; a prompt is stored only when you save it. Your name and email come from your Save My Prompts sign-in and show which account is connected.

ChatGPT's own model writes the improved prompts and templates. Save My Prompts doesn't run an AI model on your prompts.

You need a Save My Prompts account. Prompts you save here also appear in your library on savemyprompts.net and in the Save My Prompts browser extension.
defaultPrompt: Improve this prompt: write a LinkedIn post about our new product
Find my saved prompts about email
Turn what we just did into a reusable prompt template

positive.description: Improves a weak prompt and shows the result without saving it. An account can make 20 improve_prompt calls a month; after that the tool answers in plain words with the date it resets.
positive.prompt: Improve this prompt: write a LinkedIn post about our new AI product
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT writes an improved prompt and calls improve_prompt. The card shows the improved prompt with a role, audience, tone, structure and length, a "What changed" list, and "Save to My Prompts" and Copy buttons. Nothing is saved to the library.

positive.description: Writes an email and turns the approach into a reusable template.
positive.prompt: Write a short cold email introducing our design agency to a startup founder, then turn the approach into a reusable prompt template I can save.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT writes the cold email, then calls extract_prompt with a template it wrote from that approach. The card shows the template with {{VARIABLES}} for the parts that change (for example {{CLIENT_NAME}} and {{SERVICE}}) and a "Save as reusable prompt" button. Nothing is saved until the user clicks it.

positive.description: Saves a prompt the user asks to save.
positive.prompt: Save this prompt to my library: Summarise this article in 5 bullet points for a busy executive, then list 3 follow-up questions.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls save_prompt. The card says "Saved to your library" with the prompt's title. Searching for it afterwards ("find my saved prompts about executives") lists it.

positive.description: Finds saved prompts by topic. The reviewer account has 3 sample prompts, one titled "LinkedIn product announcement".
positive.prompt: Find my saved prompts about LinkedIn
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls search_prompts. The card lists the matching saved prompts, including "LinkedIn product announcement", each with a Use button.

positive.description: Brings in a relevant saved prompt without being asked, for a substantial task.
positive.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing our new analytics feature to B2B buyers
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls find_prompts with a short description of the task, sees the user's saved "LinkedIn product announcement" prompt, says in one line that they have a saved prompt for this, then calls get_prompt and uses it to write the post about the analytics feature.

negative.description: A general knowledge question that has nothing to do with prompts. No tool should be called.
Translation or small talk. No tool should be called.
The app has no delete tool. No tool should be called; ChatGPT should explain it can't delete saved prompts.

publication.release_notes: First release: improve, save, find and reuse prompts inside ChatGPT.
